points.description: States that the main advantage of passing arguments by reference is that it avoids making copies of large data structures (or of the argument) when the function is called. Equivalent wording, such as 'the data is not copied, so it saves time and memory for large objects', earns the mark.

rubric.notes: The model answer is a single idea, so the whole 5 marks sit on one all-or-nothing point. Full marks go to any answer that names avoiding copying of the argument or large data as the main advantage, in any wording. No marks go to answers that give a different advantage, such as being able to modify the caller's variable, or that describe passing by reference as making a copy.
